correctness.rationale: Re-derive the conservative stage v=(2x+t/2)/(t+2) and final scalar solve x+=(x+tw/2)/(1+t(u+w)/2) with u=x/v,w=(1-x)/(1-v). Symbolic elimination gives delta+=delta*m_t(delta^2) with positive denominator K-HD and strictly negative derivative in D. Endpoint ratios c(t)=(2-t)/(2+t), b(t)=(4-t-t²)/(t²+3t+4), so q=max(c,-b)<1 for each finite t; this proves uniform global geometric contraction. The two monotone endpoints cross at the unique positive zero of t³+2t²-2t-8, yielding optimal t. b(t)>=0 characterizes non-crossing and t=2 yields -delta³/(12-5delta²). Independently symbolic stage computation verified the map, derivative identity, endpoints and cubic equation. Positivity follows from strictly positive numerator and complement. No implication for different stage schemes or more species.

value.rationale: Published literature analyzes local versus global Patankar stability and the possibility of spurious fixed points. A global all-initial-state error bound, sharp optimal time step, non-overshoot frontier and exact cubic special step for the canonical conservative exchange scheme answer a motivated stability design question, distinct from mere positivity.

limitations: Exact arithmetic and strictly positive two-state symmetric exchange only.
General scheme-wide global stability conjectures are neither proved nor disproved.
